title: Ainsworth Opens With a Statement
body:
Ainsworth's 165.56 was the week's high score, but the real story is how they got there: Kenneth Walker III (32.6) and D'Andre Swift (31.9) combined for 64.5 points at running back - with David Montgomery (27.4) still sitting on the bench behind them. The resulting 97.06-point demolition of Zogg is the biggest Week 1-2 margin specifically in 13 years of NWL history, shattering the old Week 1-2 mark (Muenchow's 67.98-point win over Stover, 2022) by 29 points - though it's not the biggest blowout in league history overall; that's still Conlin's 127.6-point win over Zogg in Week 3, 2019. It is a career-best opening two weeks for Ainsworth personally, who'd never topped 237.9 combined through Week 2 before (2020). Zogg's day was rough top to bottom: nobody on the roster cracked 17 points, including first-round pick CeeDee Lamb (12.9), and the Chargers' Head Coach bonus actively cost them 5 points.

The league's best individual performance belonged to Caleb Williams (37.3) - an 8th-round pick who outscored every quarterback drafted ahead of him and powered Muenchow past Pfaffinger, 133.46-95.3. Glaser's 152.9 (2nd-best team score of the week) rode Derrick Henry (34.8) and Christian Watson (29.7) past Palaia, while 11th-round pick Jalen Coker quietly dropped 29.8 from the bench - a lineup call that didn't end up mattering in a 48-point win. Conlin needed just 129.86 to handle Hagan (78.02), with Josh Allen's 35.7 the league's second-best individual number of the week.

The nightcap was the only real nail-biter: Larson held off Prodahl 101.86-87.92, a 13.94-point margin. Goetz beat Stover 108.06-85.46 behind Jahmyr Gibbs (31.1), the draft's own first overall pick, to round out the slate.

Six games, five double-digit margins, and a Week 1-2 scoring record on the books - Week 1 wasted no time separating the contenders from the rest.

title: Zogg Bounces Back, Three Teams Start 2-0
body:
A week after absorbing the biggest Week 1-2 beating in 13 years of NWL history, Zogg answered with the week's high score - 138.86 - led by CeeDee Lamb (31.3, more than double his Week 1 output) and 11th-round pick Dak Prescott (29.8), to knock off Goetz (75.6) and get back in the win column. The response looks dramatic, but the numbers say otherwise: Zogg's 207.4 combined two-week total is almost exactly their 13-year career average (207.1) for this point in a season - Week 1 was the outlier, not Week 2.

Ainsworth, Glaser, and Larson all won again to open the season 2-0, the only unbeaten teams left in the league - though it means very different things for each of them. Ainsworth's 283.8 and Glaser's 265.9 are both career bests through two weeks, blowing past their previous personal highs (237.9 and 207.4, both set in 2020) by 86-94 points. Larson's 203.5, by contrast, is almost dead-even with their own career average - proof that this league's power rankings (which weigh scoring and all-play expected wins, not just the win-loss record) have them 3rd rather than 1st for a reason.

Hagan bounced back from a rough Week 1 to beat Pfaffinger 105.06-70.9, even after starting Jalen Hurts (16.2) over a Brock Purdy (28.5, a 13th-round pick) sitting on the bench - a decision that would have flipped a closer game. Pfaffinger's own Bryce Young, picked up as a free agent the same week, delivered 24.1 points in his Pfaffinger debut. Larson handled Palaia 101.68-58.84 - the week's lowest score - behind Patrick Mahomes' 29.0.

The closest game of the week came at the bottom of the standings: Prodahl edged Stover 84.92-72.98, an 11.94-point margin. Through two weeks, Pfaffinger, Palaia, and Stover are all 0-2, and the gap between the top and bottom of the league is already starting to show.

title: Glaser Stays Perfect, Benches Decide Week 3
body:
Glaser is 3-0 again. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (30.4) and Derrick Henry (21.4) carried a 113.14-106.34 win over Larson, even with Kenyon Sadiq (20.0) and Juwan Johnson (19.3) on the bench while Dalton Schultz started and scored 4.5. Glaser also opened 2025 at 3-0, which makes them the first manager in NWL history to start back-to-back seasons 3-0 - none of the 17 teams that started 3-0 from 2013-2025 had ever done it twice in a row. History is encouraging: 16 of those 17 made the playoffs. The one that didn't was Conlin in 2018, who started 3-0 and still finished 7th. Last year's 3-0 Glaser only finished 6th, so nobody should print the banner yet.

The loudest part of Week 3 was the benches. Larson lost that game by 6.80 with Michael Wilson (20.4) and Terry McLaurin (16.7) on the bench while Devaughn Vele (5.4) started. The Wilson-for-Vele swap alone was worth 15 points. Ainsworth, the league's leading scorer at 382.9 points, lost 101.28-99.10 to Stover in the closest game of the season. Ainsworth's Ravens Head Coach scored +5 on the bench, so starting the coach wins it by 2.82. Stover's first win of the year came partly from Kalif Raymond (18.0) in the flex, a sentence nobody had on their bingo card.

Hagan did it the other way around. Brock Purdy scored 31.3, the most by any quarterback in the league this week, from Hagan's bench, while Jalen Hurts started and scored 12.6. Hagan won anyway, 85.62-68.84, because the opponent was Zogg. Zogg has now scored under 70 twice in three weeks (68.50 in Week 1, 68.84 here), with the Week 2 high score of 138.86 in between. The Bengals Head Coach cost them 5 points. That's 7 sub-70 regular-season games for Zogg since the current scoring era started in 2022. Hagan is 2-1 despite a negative point differential (268.7 for, 269.6 against).

Palaia put up the week's high score, 132.16, behind Bijan Robinson (34.3) and Brock Bowers (22.6), and beat Pfaffinger by 59.02. Pfaffinger opened 2025 at 3-0 and is now 0-3. It's their third 0-3 start (2020, 2022, 2026), tied with Hagan, Goetz, and Larson for the most in league history. Pfaffinger's 370.7 points against lead the league by 42.5 and rank 9th-most through three weeks in NWL history. None of the 18 teams that started 0-3 from 2013-2025 won a title, and only 4 made the playoffs. Still, Pfaffinger has escaped this before: the 2020 team faced 394.8 points in its first three games (2nd-most ever), started 0-3, and finished 5th.

Elsewhere: Jahmyr Gibbs scored 37.9, the most of any player this week, and Goetz beat Prodahl 121.34-103.86. Prodahl started Drake Maye (3.8) with Kyler Murray (10.4) on the bench. Muenchow handled Conlin 102.50-81.06 behind Garrett Wilson (21.7) and Matthew Stafford (20.9). Conlin left Jordan Addison (17.5) on the bench and has now lost two straight.

Week 4's headliner is #1 vs. #2: Glaser hosts Ainsworth with ESPN favoring Glaser by 11. The all-time series is tied 12-12, and their last meeting (Week 10, 2025) went to Ainsworth 113.54-112.20. The week's biggest spread belongs to Prodahl, favored by 18 over Zogg.
